title: Two independent Discord (and two Pushover) configurations on the same page; filling one leaves the other's Test saying it is unconfigured
summary: The Notifications page rendered a legacy app_settings-backed 'Discord' section AND a keyring-backed 'Discord (routing matrix)' section (same for Pushover), each with its own store and Test button. Root cause fixed by collapsing to ONE configuration per transport: the keyring-backed section is now titled plainly 'Discord'/'Pushover' and is the only one rendered locally; it ADOPTS any legacy plaintext webhook/token into the keyring config on load, and keeps the legacy keys in step on save (only when they already hold a value, so the pre-router NotificationService keeps firing at the webhook that is on screen and no new plaintext copy of a bearer token is ever created). The legacy rows survive only on a remote controller, where the keyring lives on the host and the settings remote-sync is the only reachable path.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/notification_single_transport_config_test.dart — pumps the real NotificationSettings page and asserts one 'Discord'/'Pushover' heading, one credential field each, and that the legacy plaintext values really landed in the keyring-backed provider + SecretsStore.
revert_check: 1) notification_settings.dart: `if (isRemoteController)` -> `if (true)` on the legacy Discord SettingsSection => test 1 fails 'Found 2 widgets with text "Discord"'. 2) discord_transport_section.dart: `if (cfg.webhookUrl.isEmpty &&` -> `if (false &&` on the adoption block => test 2 fails Expected 'https://discord.com/api/webhooks/111/LEGACY' Actual ''. Both restored; 43 tests green.
needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/notification_service.dart:295 and :358 still send Discord/Pushover from the plaintext app_settings keys. Once that service reads discordTransportConfigProvider / pushoverTransportConfigProvider (or drops its direct sends now that notify() forwards to the router), the legacy keys and the mirror-write in the two transport sections can be deleted, and secrets_store.dart migrateFromPlaintext can absorb the adoption so it no longer depends on the user opening the Notifications page.
caveats: A remote controller still shows the legacy rows because it cannot reach the host keyring (NotificationRoutingSettings already declares those transports host-owned there). Adoption runs when the Notifications page is opened, not at startup — the legacy value keeps working until then, so nothing goes dark in the interim.

title: Auto-Save Status reports 'Last backup: Never' while a backup from 20 minutes earlier in the same session exists
summary: Already fixed on this working tree (uncommitted, last committed state was 6.0.0). auto_save_settings.dart now watches autoSaveLifecycleProvider (the only provider that loads the persisted autosave.* keys and calls start(config, lastBackup)) and reads status from `ref.watch(autoSaveStatusProvider).valueOrNull ?? service.status` at line 193 — autoSaveStatusProvider is the hydrating provider the finding named, and it is the same source Settings > Backup & Restore reads, so the two surfaces can no longer disagree. The file is also outside my ownership list, so I did not touch it.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart — 'Status shows the persisted last backup, not "Never"' seeds autosave.last_backup_at 2h back, overrides autoSaveServiceProvider with an UN-STARTED service (exactly the stale instance the old code rendered), and asserts find.text('2h ago') findsOneWidget plus 'Never' and 'Pending' findsNothing. 3 tests, green.
revert_check: Not performed destructively: the file is owned by another agent this run and a temporary edit could clobber a concurrent write. The existing test severs the wiring by construction — it hands the widget the un-hydrated autoSaveServiceProvider instance, so any revert to `ref.read(autoSaveServiceProvider).status` renders 'Never'/'Pending' and fails all three assertions.
caveats: Verified by inspection + running the existing suite, not by an actual revert.

title: Editing a settings dropdown fires a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' alert on a completely idle app, and the alert text contradicts itself
summary: Confirmed real and NOT yet fixed (both cited files are clean in git). Cause is entirely in skotiq_core, outside my ownership list. (a) weather_safety_provider.dart:879 — _enforceSafetyActions only skips SafeRig when none of shouldPause/shouldPark/shouldCloseDome is set; it never asks whether there is anything to safe, so enabling weather safety with no weather source resolves fail-closed to unsafe+shouldPark and really runs the safing routine on an idle app (matching the observed 'Secondary rig stopped' log line). (b) safe_rig_service.dart:498/504 — when no step ran, detail is 'no action was possible' and it is still interpolated into 'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: $detail.', which asserts the rig was safed and that nothing happened in one sentence. Nothing in the settings widget I own (weather_safety_settings.dart just calls _updateSettings) can fix either without being a disclosure-only patch, which the brief forbids.
test: None written — the fix belongs to files I may not edit; writing a test against unchanged behaviour would only pin the defect.
needs_shared_change: TWO edits, both in skotiq_core. (1) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/weather_safety_provider.dart, _enforceSafetyActions, extend the early return at line 879: also skip SafeRig (and return true so the episode latches) when there is nothing to safe — sequenceExecutionStateProvider is not pausable AND mountStateProvider / domeStateProvider / cover / cameraStateProvider are all disconnected. The correct disclosure for that state already exists at lines 763-774 (the warning-severity failModeWarning toast), so gating the escalation leaves the operator informed without a red CRITICAL. (2) packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/safe_rig_service.dart, _emitNotification lines 494-507: when `steps.isEmpty`, stop emitting 'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: no action was possible.' — use showWarning with 'Nothing to safe: no run was active and no mount, dome or cover is connected.' (keeping the existing mountAbsent gap sentence). Keep showError/CRITICAL for result.hasFailures and for the case where steps actually ran. Suggested test: a container with no connected devices and an idle sequencer, flipping weatherSafetyEnabled true with no weather source, asserting uiNotificationProvider received a warning and NOT an error titled 'Safe the rig', and that safeRigServiceProvider.safeTheRig was never called.
caveats: Reproduction was not re-run live; the diagnosis is from reading the two cited call paths, which match the verifier's log evidence exactly.
